Soojin / Rishi,

Thanks for the heads-up and the attached redline. Below is a suggested position for each of the Acme asks — I flagged language to insert into the Order Form and a rationale you can share with the customer. I'll prepare a tracked-changes doc (OF_ACME_v3_tracked_changes.docx) and clean PDF for the call.

1) Net terms
- Position: Offer Net 45 for this customer on the Order Form (replace the 30-day default). Add a clause that an invoice for any onboarding or one-time integration fees shall be due Net 30 to ease cashflow and reduce credit exposure.
- Rationale: Accepting Net 45 is acceptable for a strategic expansion when accompanied by an onboarding Net 30 invoice and standard late-fee and interest language. This balances Acme's AP constraint with Redwood's DSO risk.

2) Taxes
- Position: Insert explicit tax clause: "Prices are exclusive of taxes. Customer shall be responsible for all sales, use, value-added, or other similar taxes imposed on the purchase of Services, except for taxes based on Redwood's net income. If Redwood is required by law to collect tax, Customer shall reimburse Redwood. Where Customer claims exemption, Customer shall provide appropriate documentation."
- Rationale: This is standard; do not accept gross-up requests unless finance confirms material exposure. If Acme pushes for gross-up, require evidence and escalate for finance sign-off.

3) Minimum commit / ramp
- Position: Accept the proposed ramp: Year 1 commit $350k, Year 2 commit $500k. Add an annual true-up mechanism and a usage-linked uplift clause: "If Customer exceeds the committed spend in any quarter by more than 25%, parties will automatically convert to a higher pricing tier for the following quarter subject to mutual agreement." Also include early-termination remedy: if Customer fails to meet 80% of the annual committed spend, Redwood may invoice the shortfall or apply a credit reduction.
- Rationale: The ramp keeps the deal moving while protecting Redwood via true-ups and shortfall remedies.

4) Invoicing cadence
- Position: Maintain monthly in arrears by default but allow quarterly invoicing by exception. Add a clause: "Invoices issued monthly and payable within the applicable Net terms. Customer may request quarterly invoicing; Redwood will accommodate provided payment timeline is not extended beyond agreed Net terms."

5) Next steps and tactical asks
- I'll prepare tracked changes and a clean PDF for the call.
- Rishi: please confirm we can accept the Net 45 concession and the proposed shortfall recovery remedies (invoice shortfall or credit).
- Soojin: suggest you share this language with Jordan and propose a 30-minute alignment call at 11:00am PT tomorrow. If they push for gross-up or any tax registration obligations in multiple states, escalate to me and I'll loop in tax counsel.

Regards,
Monica Patel
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.inference.com
